- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.  
- If sentiment shows strong bearish momentum (≥0.33) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 18-day history shows volatility, apply smoothing: average last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment’s direction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish signals (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.33 or lower), model underperforms; apply 2–4% upward correction to avoid false bottoms.
